evidence.excerpt: Inferring gene regulatory networks from observational transcriptomic data is complicated when sample sizes are small relative to the number of candidate variables. This study evaluated four score-based structure learning algorithms—BDe, BGe, BIC-penalised hill-climbing, and a tabu-search variant—on RNA-seq data from 18 Arabidopsis thaliana samples subjected to 4°C cold stress over 24 hours. We assessed edge recovery against a manually curated reference subnetwork of 42 known regulatory interactions. The BGe criterion with a conservative prior on graph complexity recovered 61% of true edges at a false discovery rate of 0.18, outperforming BIC-penalised search (52% recovery, FDR 0.24). We also examined sensitivity to prior specification by varying hyperparameters across a grid of 120 settings. Results indicate that informative priors derived from published protein–protein interaction data improve skeleton accuracy by approximately 9 percentage points in this low-n regime. Data and scoring code are deposited in a public repository.
